info.name: asyncdb
info.description:
The key journeys of the asyncdb HTTP/JSON API, in the order a client lives them: declare the table graph, write and read records, scan and page a range, find that a record cannot be erased, drop the table. Folders 1 to 7 run against one instance; folder 8 runs against the three of docker-compose.

Run the whole collection with the runner or with newman — the requests depend on the ones before them, and folder 0 makes a re-run start from a clean table.

Every assertion is drawn from doc/database, which is the spec: the codes are the documented codes, the statuses the documented statuses.

item.name: 3 · The record lifecycle
item.description: One key, one value, and the three operations most clients will ever use. A value is bytes the service never looks at, the empty value is a value, and a missing key is told from it by the status code. Nothing here erases a record: a value that should not be read again is overwritten, and the key stays until the table goes.

item.name: 6 · Records cannot be erased
item.description: There is no delete of a key and no delete of a range: both are 405, and a table is dropped whole or not at all. What that buys is a store with no tombstones in it — nothing a scan has to read again until a compaction takes it away.

item.name: A delete of a range is not a method of the route
Nor is a delete of one key
The partition folder 5 seeded is still whole

7 · Drop the tables
item.description: The cheap way to delete a lot of data: the column family goes and the data goes with it. A table that is not there is 404, and the records of a dropped table are gone even where the table is created again.

8 · The cluster
item.description:
Only for the three instances of docker-compose, addressed by node1, node2 and node3. Every node answers for every key: a table is created on all of them, a record is served by the node that owns its key whichever node was asked, and a scan is asked of every node and merged back into key order.

Running this folder against a single instance fails at the first request, which is the point — it is asserting that there is a cluster.

exec: // An instance that joined no cluster names no nodes at all, and the rest of this folder
// still runs: node1, node2 and node3 are then the one instance, and every request is
// answered where it lands rather than forwarded. Only the membership is unassertable.
pm.test("skipped: one instance names no membership, so run this folder against a cluster", function () {
pm.test("the node names the cluster as it sees it", function () {
pm.expect(body.nodes, "no nodes: this instance is standing alone").to.be.an("array");
pm.test("the node is registered in the etcd it read that membership from", function () {
pm.expect(body.etcd, "no etcd: this instance was told none").to.be.an("object");
